title: The Triangle Inequality Theorem

key_big: Any two sides add to more than the third.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Triangle Inequality Theorem: the sum of any two sides is greater than the third side.
  • Check the two shortest sides against the longest.
  • If two sides are a and b, the third side is between |a − b| and a + b.
  • The longest side is opposite the largest angle.

Examples

Example

Sides 5 and 9

9 − 5 = 4

9 + 5 = 14

Answer: 4 < x < 14

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Checking only one pairCheck the two shortest against the longest.
Including the endpointsEqual to the sum makes a flat line.
Largest angle opposite the shortest sideIt is opposite the longest side.
